data.gender_notes: Masahir is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic root 'sa-ha-ra', meaning 'to observe'. Masahir refers to a wise observer or someone who is attentive and mindful of their surroundings. The name Masahir carries the meaning “Wise observer” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Masahir usually hope their child will grow to embody wise observer and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.etymology: Masahir belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Wise observer.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Masahir total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

They were individuals known for their deep understanding of various aspects of life, from science to literature to religion. Masahir played a crucial role in preserving and transmitting knowledge through generations, making them a valuable asset to Islamic society.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, Masahir is a reminder of the importance of observation, reflection, and mindfulness in our daily lives. The name encourages us to pay attention to the world around us and seek knowledge and wisdom from it. Masahir also highlights the value of being present and attentive in every moment, which is vital for spiritual growth and development.
